The shell and head thickness (𝑡 ) are calculated as follows, based on ASME Boiler 𝑣𝑒𝑠𝑠𝑒𝑙 and Pressure Vessel code (BPVC) guidelines [29]: 𝑃 ×𝐷 𝑡 = 𝑣𝑒𝑠𝑠𝑒𝑙 𝑣𝑒𝑠𝑠𝑒𝑙 +𝐶𝑅 ×𝑁 (4) 𝑣𝑒𝑠𝑠𝑒𝑙 𝑦 2×𝑆×𝑊×𝐸−1.2𝑃 Here, 𝑃 is the combined ullage and hydrostatic pressure. The vapor pressure of 𝑣𝑒𝑠𝑠𝑒𝑙 sulfur at the top temperature of 300°C is ~1 psi [31] (sulfur boiling point: 444°C) and so its contribution to the vessel pressure is minimal. 𝐶𝑅 is the corrosion rate for the stainless- steel alloy used, and 𝑁 is the system lifetime of 30 years, 𝑊 is the strength reduction 𝑦 factor, 𝐸 is the joint efficiency and 𝑆 is the maximum allowable stress of the shell material at the design temperature of 300°C. Joint efficiency is a factor required in all head and shell calculations that accounts for how closely a finished weld joint approximates the quality of the seamless parent material. ASME Section VIII [29] provides guidelines for joint efficiency values to be used based on the degree of radiographic examination. The Page 38 of 87 DE-EE0009329 Element 16 Technologies, Inc. inspection scope considered here includes spot radiography on both the longitudinal and circumferential seams of the vessel. Consequently, as mandated by ASME Section VIII code, a joint efficiency of 0.85 was applied for the longitudinal welds in the shell and head to determine the minimum required wall thickness. Since vessels are generally fabricated from metal plates and only available in discrete sizes, the final vessel thickness is obtained by rounding up the value obtained from Eq. (4) to the next available increment. The vessel volume (𝑉 ) depends on the TES storage capacity (𝑄 ) and the 𝑣𝑒𝑠𝑠𝑒𝑙 𝑇𝐸𝑆 fraction of volume occupied by the inert gas blanket at the top of the vessel (𝜐 ), 𝑢𝑙𝑙𝑎𝑔𝑒 termed as ullage. Element 16 typically designs the storage vessel for a maximum ullage pressure rating of 40 psig. Based on the volume expansion of molten sulfur cycling between 200°C and 300°C, and the compressibility of the inert gas, we determined that the ullage fraction (𝜐 ), should be approximately 8% when the bulk sulfur is in its 𝑢𝑙𝑙𝑎𝑔𝑒 molten state at 120°C.
